title: Break IR0
subtitle: Cause a failure. Guess what happens first — then walk what the machine actually does.

hook.prompt: You forced a panic. What happens first?

options.text: Only that process dies; the shell continues.
The kernel stops. It will not keep running.

sequence.label: Something is unrecoverable
sequence.user: The machine stops being usable. No prompt comes back.
sequence.kernel: A subsystem calls panic() — the kernel will not continue.

sequence.label: Framebuffer clears
sequence.user: The screen goes to a panic banner. Serial noise stays off this path.
sequence.kernel: GUI panic path paints a dedicated surface, not the klog dump.
sequence.image_alt: IR0 panic banner on the framebuffer

sequence.label: Readable failure
sequence.user: Uptime, fault site, and a short shutdown hint.
sequence.kernel: Serial/klog still get the register dump and stack for developers.

sequence.label: Halt
sequence.user: The box sits there. You reboot.

hook.prompt: A program touches a bad address. What happens first?

options.text: The CPU raises a page fault.

sequence.label: Bad address
sequence.user: A program touches memory it must not.
sequence.kernel: The CPU raises #PF. CR2 holds the address.

sequence.label: Classify the fault
sequence.user: Nothing on screen yet — the kernel is still deciding.
sequence.kernel: pf_user_segv: userspace, not present or forbidden.

sequence.label: SIGSEGV
sequence.kernel: Default action kills the task. wait status is WIFSIGNALED.

sequence.label: Shell continues
sequence.user: Segmentation fault — then the prompt is back.
sequence.kernel: Parent wait4 reaps the child. PID 1 / the shell keeps running.

hook.prompt: You sent SIGKILL. What happens first?

options.text: The process can catch it and keep running.
The kernel queues a signal that cannot be caught.

sequence.label: You send the signal
sequence.kernel: sys_kill queues SIGKILL. It cannot be caught.

sequence.label: Default kill
sequence.kernel: process_signal_default_kill → exit. A zombie waits for wait4.

sequence.label: Prompt returns
sequence.kernel: The parent reaps. Job-control UX vs the exit path.

hook.prompt: cat is sitting there with no input. Where is it?

options.text: Finished; the shell just looks idle.
Asleep in the kernel, blocked on read(0).

sequence.label: Blocked in the kernel
sequence.user: cat sits there. No line, no return.
sequence.kernel: read(0) sleeps: PROCESS_BLOCKED on TTY input.

sequence.label: Ctrl+C
sequence.kernel: SIGINT. The waiter is woken; the syscall does not finish normally.

sequence.label: EINTR
sequence.user: The command dies. You get the prompt.
sequence.kernel: Interrupted syscall returns EINTR — restart or error, by the caller.

scenarios.title: Fill a pipe
scenarios.command: writer vs a full pipe buffer

hook.prompt: The writer is faster than the reader. What happens when the pipe fills?

sequence.label: Producer writes
sequence.user: A program writes faster than anyone reads.
sequence.kernel: Bytes land in the pipe buffer.

sequence.label: Buffer is full
sequence.kernel: pipe full → block the writer (or EAGAIN if O_NONBLOCK).

sequence.label: Consumer reads
sequence.kernel: A read wakes the writer. Both ends keep a refcount.
